learning_objective: 🎯 Understand what a constitution is, why society needs it, and how the Indian Constitution was crafted by the Constituent Assembly!

main_concepts.concept_title: 📜 Why do we need a Constitution?
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A constitution provides a set of basic rules that allow for minimal coordination amongst members of a society. It specifies who has the power to make decisions and sets limits on what a government can impose on its citizens.

The Constitution determines how the government will be constituted and who will have the authority to enact laws. In a democracy, this power fundamentally rests with the people through their elected representatives.
The Constitution restricts the power of the government by guaranteeing certain fundamental rights to the citizens that no government can ever violate.
It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly (formed in 1946). The makers spent almost 3 years in deep deliberation, ensuring diverse voices were heard, heavily inspired by the nationalist movement.
Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946, it laid down the underlying philosophy of the Constitution, declaring India as an Independent Sovereign Republic committed to justice, equality, and freedom.

fun_activity.title: 📝 Frame Your Own Rules
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are starting a new club at school. Write down 5 core rules (a mini-constitution) that every member, including the president of the club, must follow. See how hard it is to make rules everyone agrees on!

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember the 4 main functions of a constitution: coordination, decision-making powers, limiting government, and fulfilling aspirations.
📌 Be ready to explain the 'Objective Resolution' and who introduced it (Jawaharlal Nehru).
📌 Note the borrowing of provisions (e.g., Fundamental Rights from USA, Parliamentary system from UK) but emphasize that it was an adaptation, not a blind copy.
quick_recap: ⭐ A Constitution is the supreme law of the land.
⭐ The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950.
⭐ It is a document born out of a successful national movement, carrying the aspirations of millions.
